The base template: menus, death and fallbacks

New games are seeded with editable boilerplate before the first room. Use it as a recommended starting point when it fits, or extend or replace any part to serve the brief. These are ordinary game resources, with no protected ownership or reserved template ranges.

- Logic 0 builds the menu bar once on boot (File: Save, Restore, Restart, Quit; Speed; Sound; Help), binds the classic keys (ESC opens the menu, F5/F7/F9 save, restore and restart, F1 shows help, TAB lists the inventory), turns the status line on, then runs call.v(v0) so your room logic runs first every cycle. After the room returns, logic 0 answers the menu controllers and, once per submitted line, prints the parser fallback: "I don't know the word" when the line carried an unknown word, "I don't understand that" when no said() matched. A room that answers a line without a said() match should set(f4) after its own reply so the template does not add the generic one.
- Death is a shared handler: print your death line, then call(255). It stops input and movement, plays the death sound and offers the Restore, Restart or Quit box — SPACE steps the choice, ENTER confirms, 1-3 choose directly, F7/F9/Alt-Z answer directly. A cancelled or failed restore returns to the box; the player stays dead rather than walking in a broken control mode. If you replace this handler, design and playtest the recovery or continuation behavior your game needs.
- Read logic 0 and logic 255 for their current state, controller and string usage before editing; their sources are available through read_logic. Update affected references together when reusing IDs or changing conventions. Automatic allocation avoids IDs used by the current code; explicit bindings and edits can coordinate a rewrite. Playtest boot, input and any menu/death behavior affected by your changes. A fair death still needs a fair cause: the hazard belongs in your room's picture and priority plane.

rooms.title: Precinct Front Desk
rooms.description: Millhaven PD lobby. Sergeant Prakash gives Dana the Hale's Pharmacy assignment and a camera; the bulletin board repeats the details. Dana returns here at the end to write, sign and file the arrest report with the evidence.

exits.name: east glass doors to Main Street

rooms.title: Records Office
rooms.description: Filing cabinets and the Harbor Properties lease ledger. With the driver's logbook entry (Pier Rd #7) and the pharmacist's account of a Quickline van, Dana finds Warehouse 7 is leased to Gil Voss and takes the ledger page.

rooms.title: Main Street
rooms.description: Red-brick shopfronts, the blue-and-white patrol car with Officer Bud Bukowski, and delivery driver Marty Voss by his Quickline van. Checking his logbook against his story exposes the discrepancy.

rooms.title: Hale's Pharmacy
rooms.description: Broken front window, glass on the sidewalk side. Dana photographs the scene, bags an empty pill bottle (lot LN-4471) by the back door and hears pharmacist Ruth Okafor, who is frightened of Quickline, describe a Quickline van out back at 1:50 a.m.

rooms.title: Pier Road Warehouse
rooms.description: Warehouse 7 on the pier. Bud warns Dana not to go in alone; entering without backup ends the case. After radioing dispatch for backup, Dana arrests Gil Voss with the stolen case of lot LN-4471.

facts.name: case
facts.text: Hale's Pharmacy on Main Street was broken into about 2 a.m.; a case of prescription painkillers was stolen. Marty Voss of Quickline Delivery reported it at 2:15 a.m., claiming he drove past and saw a stranger in a gray hoodie smash the window.

facts.name: discrepancy
facts.text: Marty's Quickline logbook shows his last stop at 11:40 p.m. (Pier Rd #7, 'returns pickup') and van check-in at the depot at 12:05 a.m. He was not on a route at 2 a.m. The logbook is inventory item 4.

facts.name: scene_evidence
facts.text: At the pharmacy the window glass lies outside (broken from inside, staged). An empty pill bottle, lot LN-4471, lies by the back door (item 5). Photographing the scene gives crime scene photos (item 6). Pharmacist Ruth Okafor saw a Quickline van out back at 1:50 a.m.; Quickline threatened her over 'missing boxes'.

facts.name: records_link
facts.text: The Harbor Properties lease ledger in records shows Warehouse 7 on Pier Road leased to Gil Voss, Marty's brother. Taking the ledger page gives item 7.

facts.name: culprit
facts.text: Gil Voss broke in; Marty drove lookout and invented the stranger. Gil is in Warehouse 7 with the stolen case (lot LN-4471). Arrest requires backup via radio to dispatch.

facts.name: npcs
facts.text: Sergeant Prakash (front desk, three trays: IN, OUT, WRONG TRAY; dry). Officer Bud Bukowski (partner at the patrol car on Main Street, talkative, brave; warns Dana before the warehouse). Dispatch (radio, patient, dry, repeats details). Ruth Okafor (pharmacist, frightened of Quickline). Marty Voss (driver). Gil Voss (suspect).

messages: Millhaven Police Department, 7:58 a.m. Officer Dana Reyes reports for her first week on patrol. Sergeant Prakash sits behind the front desk, sorting forms into three trays.
Prakash calls after you. "Reyes! You don't have an assignment yet."
"Reyes. Hale's Pharmacy on Main Street was broken into overnight. Somebody took a case of prescription painkillers."
"A delivery driver, Marty Voss, called it in at 2:15 this morning. Says he saw the whole thing. He's waiting by his van on Main Street. Take his statement."

"Then document the scene. Photographs, and anything the thief left behind." He slides a department camera across the counter. "Bukowski is riding with you. He's out at the car. Try to keep him on topic."
"The details are on the board if you forget. Dismissed."
The yellow card reads: HALE'S PHARMACY, MAIN ST. BREAK-IN APPROX. 2 A.M. REPORTED 2:15 A.M. BY MARTY VOSS, QUICKLINE DELIVERY. TAKE STATEMENT. DOCUMENT SCENE.
